meta.title: Mexico's history sounds made up — but it's real
meta.source: User script (verbatim; citation markers removed). Sources: Guinness World Records (shortest presidency), Cornell Library 'When Money Grew on Trees', Wikipedia Great Pyramid of Cholula, NYT 1952, Mental Floss.

scenes.name: Hook

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mexico’s history sounds made up—but these facts are real.

spoken: Mexico's history sounds made up, but these facts are real.
scenes.note: Three facts that sound made up

scenes.name: 45-minute president

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One president, Pedro Lascuráin, held office for less than an hour in 1913. That’s shorter than your lunch break.

spoken: One president, Pedro Lass-koo-rah-een, held office for less than an hour in nineteen thirteen. That's shorter than your lunch break.

scenes.name: Cacao money

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Aztecs used cacao beans as money. Imagine accidentally drinking your savings.

spoken: The Aztecs used cacao beans as money. Imagine accidentally drinking your savings.
scenes.note: Cacao beans were currency in Aztec markets

scenes.name: Pyramid of Cholula

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the world’s largest pyramid by volume? It’s not in Egypt—it’s in Cholula, Mexico. Today, a church sits on top.

spoken: And the world's largest pyramid by volume? It's not in Egypt, it's in Cholula, Mexico. Today, a church sits on top.
scenes.note: Great Pyramid of Cholula — largest by volume; church on top

scenes.name: Recap

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A speed-run presidency, edible money, and a pyramid hiding beneath a church. Mexico’s history does not disappoint.

spoken: A speed-run presidency, edible money, and a pyramid hiding beneath a church. Mexico's history does not disappoint.
